newsitem.title: FRANCE: Shakeup looms if Alcatel wins Thomson bid - paper.
newsitem.headline: Shakeup looms if Alcatel wins Thomson bid - paper.

text.p: French telecommuniations and engineering group Alcatel Alsthom plans to shut Thomson Multimedia's U.S. factories if it is sucessful in its bid for the company, the Financial Times of London reported on Tuesday.
The French government was expected to decide by mid-October whether to sell Thomson SA to Alcatel or to the French defence and media company Lagardere group.
Thomson consists of two parts -- Thomson Multimedia, a consumer electronics company, and Thomson CSF, a defence manufacturer.
The newspaper said that Alcatel's plan would be part of an effort to turn around the loss-making group.
It said Alcatel also planned to rationalise Thomson Multimedia's six brands in Europe to cut the cost of marketing and support.

It added that Alcatel was considering whether to manage Thomson Multimedia from France. The newspaper said that one possiblity would be to run the company from the U.S. given that most of its sales were there.

If Alcatel won the contest for Thomson, it planned to sell a majority of Thomson Multimedia to a partner specialising in consumer electronics, the newspaper said. The group would then not be required to consolidate all of Thomson Multimedia's 14 billion francs in debts on its balance sheet.
The newspaper said that Alcatel expected to press ahead with Thomson Multimedia's restructuring if it won the Thomson battle on the grounds that it would be important to cut costs quickly.
